jia: Heads-up — onboarding a HF gpt-like model and seeing a small but consistent quality dip after conversion + quant. Suspect tokenizer normalizer differences (unicode + byte-fallback + whitespace).

sam: How small? exact metric drop?

jia: ~1.8% on our pass@1 on the unit tests and hallucination rate up on a handful of prompts. Token counts differ for ~12% of eval prompts.

lina: Did you compare HF tokenizer config.json vs the one our conversion script writes? special_tokens?

jia: Yep. special_tokens match. But HF has a normalizer section with "name": "nfc" in some ckpts, and others use "nfkc_cf". Our conversion currently forces NFKC.

ben: That could explain whitespace/nbsp handling. NF(C/K)C can fold non-breaking spaces and compatibility chars differently.

jia: Repro steps I ran:

```
from tokenizers import Tokenizer
hf = Tokenizer.from_file('hf_tokenizer.json')
hf.encode("hello world") -> tokens: ["hello", " world"]
red = Tokenizer.from_file('redwood_conv.json')
red.encode("hello world") -> tokens: ["hello world"]
```

jia: So hf split NBSP, our conv merged. That changes prefix caching and sometimes leading space tokens in chat templates.

sam: Did you check byte-fallback/prenorm? some HF tokenizers use byte fallback pretokenizer which preserves odd bytes, ours uses unicode pretokenization with fallback later.

jia: I printed the pretokenizer config too:

```
HF: {"pre_tokenizer": [{"Split": {...}}, {"ByteLevel": {"add_prefix_space": false}}], "normalizer": {"NFKC": ...}}
Red: {"pre_tokenizer": [{"WhitespaceSplit": {} }], "normalizer": {"NFKC": ...}}
```

lina: So ByteLevel add_prefix_space vs WhitespaceSplit mismatch -> chat-mode templates that rely on leading space tokens (" Hello" vs "Hello") will change tokenization. That breaks our chat formatting and some evals.

ben: Quick experiment: force add_prefix_space=true in conversion and run token-diff on dev prompts. If diffs drop, we found the cause.

jia: Did that. add_prefix_space=true fixed ~70% of token-count mismatches but NBSP difference remained.

sam: For NBSP maybe the HF normalizer used "nfc" whereas our global NFKC fold is coalescing NBSP into normal space. We should preserve the tokenizer's declared normalizer rather than overriding.

jia: Agreed. I dug into tokenizer.normalizer serialized field — HF sometimes emits nested normalizer ops like Sequence([NFC, StripAccents]) which our parser flattens to single NFKC. That loses op order semantics.

lina: Proposed short term fix: in conversion tool, preserve the original normalizer spec as-is (serialize verbatim) and set a flag to run tests. Longer term: add a small pretokenizer shim that canonicalizes NBSP ->   only when model card explicitly lists compatibility normalization.

ben: Also check special_tokens like "</s>" vs "</s>﻿" weird hidden zero-width chars. We had a previous regression where ZWJ sneaked into pad token.

jia: Found one example: hf tokenizer had "eos_token": "</s>​" (zero width space) in a broken upload. Our converter stripped zero-width chars quietly. That changed token ids.

sam: Oof. Can we add a linter that flags non-printable chars in special tokens? quick regex check during conversion.

lina: Yes. I'll add a rule: if special token contains codepoint category Cc, Cf, then fail conversion unless allow_hidden_tokens=true.

deploy-bot: conversion-pipeline/job-7743 status: queued -> running

jia: For reproducible evaluation I ran token diffs:

```
python tools/token_diff.py --hf hf_tokenizer.json --redwood redwood_conv.json --sample eval_prompts.txt
# output: 124/1024 prompts differ; common diffs: leading-space-token, nbsp, zero-width
```

jia: Next steps I'm going to: 1) revert forced NFKC override, 2) wire add_prefix_space from ByteLevel if present, 3) add linter for invisible chars, 4) re-run quant + eval.

ben: Also add a unit test that compares tokenization after roundtrip conversion (hf -> conv -> hf) and fails if token sequences differ for the same raw text (exact match). Keep a whitelist for known acceptable diffs with justification.

sam: If after normalizer fixes metric still falls, we might be hitting quantization sensitivity where tokenization small changes amplify generation differences. But fix tokenizer parity first.

jia: Will do. I'll push a branch and drop links to diffs and sample failing prompts in the PR.

lina: Thanks. If you want I can pair on the conversion linter tomorrow.

jia: Yes please. attaching one failing prompt here: "Summarize the paragraph: Hello world. The quick brown fox..."

ben: :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: conversion-pipeline/job-7743 status: running -> success

jia: Pipeline succeeded with updated config; running full eval now, will report results in this thread.

sam: Great, thanks for chasing this down.
